text:
alex: heads-up — after rolling keying change v2 last night I see prefix cache hit-rate drop ~12% on prod p99 traffic :eyes:

maria: who rolled v2? I thought we gated it behind canary traffic? :thinking_face:

ops-bot: deploy v2-keying -> prod completed by cheng at 1920000500 (canary=10%). No rollback recorded.

cheng: yeah I pushed the new key normalization (trim+stable-hash) to reduce KV cardinality. Canary looked fine on synthetic, weird that prod drops.

perf-bot: perf snapshot 1920000800 -> 1920001400:
- cache hit-rate (global prefix): 68% -> 56%
- median latency (tokens/sec): unchanged
- tail latency increase on cold starts (95th) +9%
- observed batch sizes shrink ~8% during high-concurrency windows

alex: exact numbers — our baseline was ~68% hit-rate for typical routes, stabilized to ~66-69. After the change it's 54-58. This aligns with higher request entropy around session prompts.

maria: could be key collision avoidance caused more distinct keys (we normalized whitespace and punctuation differently). Are we keying on truncated prefixes or whole prompt?

cheng: we switched from naive prefix substring to hashed canonical prefix: code snippet I landed:
```
func canonicalKey(p prompt) string {
  s := normalizeWhitespace(p.Prefix) // v2 change 
  if len(s) > 256 { s = s[:256] }
  return fmt.Sprintf("k:%x", sha1.Sum([]byte(s)))
}
```
This was to limit prefix length and reduce metadata growth.

sam: two quick suspects: 1) normalization increased entropy for small variations (e.g., emojis vs text) 2) autoscaler warmed nodes differently meaning fewer cached KV pages per replica. Have we correlated hit-rate drop with scaling events?

perf-bot: correlation check: 1920000600..1920001400 shows 3 autoscale up events during that window. Hit-rate drop starts immediately after first autoscale.

nora: autoscaler note — when we scale up we bring new replicas with empty KV caches; if warmers don't run or prober targets pinned prefixes we get multiplied cold-shard effect.

alex: exactly — hypothesis: our deploy-time warmers assumed old keying and used literal prefix probes. With new hashed keys the prober distribution became misaligned and didn't prime actual keys, so new replicas stayed cold.

maria: can we repro with a small cluster? Suggestions: spin a 3->6 replica upscaling test, run current prober, then run a modified prober that computes new canonicalKey and hits those keys. Compare per-replica hit-rate.

cheng: I can reproduce locally. Quick test script (pseudo):
```bash
# generate canonical keys from live sample prompts
python tools/gen_keys.py --sample last_week_prompts.json --format canonical > keys_v2.txt
# prober hits
for k in $(shuf keys_v2.txt | head -n 500); do curl -s -X POST $WARM_ENDPOINT -d "{\"key\":\"$k\"}" & done
```
This increased per-shard hit-rate from 2% to 48% in the test cluster pre-scale.

alex: good find. So two angles: fix prober to compute keys using same canonicalization; and mitigate live regressions with short-term fallback to old keying for warmers.

sam: also consider a staggered prober tied to autoscaler lifecycle: when replicas added emit a high-coverage prober for first 60s with jitter across prefixes and avoid hitting only top-n.

nora: propose scheduled nightly broad sweep as a complement — run diversity-heavy probes at 03:00 to keep warm across low-traffic hours. Use TTL-aware prober to avoid blowing cost.

maria: we should also re-evaluate batching heuristic: perf-bot showed batch sizes shrank. If warmers don't prime cache, KV misses can force shorter generation windows and break continuous batching. That amplifies tail latency.

cheng: will add a small change: when key-normalization differs between runtime and prober, log a warn with sample diff and increment a metric we can alert on.

perf-bot: added metric: warmers.key_mismatch.count (new), warmers.probe_success_ratio (new).

alex: action items:
- cheng: patch prober to use canonicalKey + enable backfill mode for last 6 hours of prefixes (owner)
- sam: design autoscaler hook that triggers targeted prober on scale events (owner)
- nora: schedule nightly diversity sweep with cost cap + TTL-aware sampling (owner)
- maria: validate batching heuristic sensitivity to cache miss rate and propose fallback (owner)
- ops: temporary run old keying-based prober for 24h while we roll out fixes (volunteer?)

ops-bot: triggered run of old-keying prober for 24h at 1920001200 per request from alex.

alex: we'll monitor hit-rate and tail latency for next 12 hours. If no improvement roll back keying change. I'll post updates here. :thumbsup:

maria: recommend adding a small synthetic traffic generator that mimics top 200 user prefixes but also injects long-tail hybrid strings to avoid overfitting warmers to top-N only.

sam: note for long-term — consider shard-aware keying where canonicalKey includes shard-id prefix when priming so probes are distributed across actual KV partitions (reduces hot-probing one replica).

cheng: ack — I'll get the prober PR up in ~2 hours and include repro script + logs.

alex: thanks everyone. If you see anomalous error spikes ping me. I'll reopen if we need rollback.

perf-bot: snapshot scheduled at 1920002400; alert if global hit-rate < 60% or 95th tail latency +10%

nora: thanks — I'll coordinate with cost to ensure sweeps stay within budget.

cheng: PR link when ready: https://git.internal/redwood/probers/pulls/452 (draft)

alex: closing loop — temporary mitigation reduced drop from 12% to 4% in the last hour. Continuing monitoring.
